But Google has included all the same great software features on the Pixel 10a that Pixel users have come to know and love. Call Assist features like Hold for Me, Direct My Call, and Call Screening are all here, and Gemini-powered favorites like Circle to Search, Magic Compose, and Audio Magic Eraser are all included, as well.

The Pixel 10a ships with Android 16 and includes seven years of promised software updates. That means you'll not only see security updates through 2033, but we expect the Pixel 10a to see Android updates through Android 23. That's a huge value add for people looking to hold on to their phone for longer!

title: Here's how long your Google Pixel phone will get software ...
text:
With the release of the Pixel 8 in 2023, Google made a widely celebrated announcement. Going forward, Pixel phones would receive seven years of software updates — not only routine security patches but major OS upgrades, too. It was a more robust promise than even Samsung, the largest vendor of Android devices, had made in 2019 when it pledged three years of major OS updates for lower-end Galaxy devices and seven for select flagships. A quick loss of software support had previously been a major reason why Android phones failed to hold their value for long, so committing to that support was crucial for the future.

...

## Newer Pixel phones get five to seven years of software updates

Google's Pixel release date page is a helpful guide here. First, all Pixels from the original model through the Pixel 5a are obsolete and no longer receiving updates.

If you have a phone in the Pixel 6 or 7 families, or the original Pixel Fold, it will receive updates for five years from the month it went on sale. That means the Pixel 7 and 7 Pro will get their final update by the end of October 2027, while the Pixel 6 and 6 Pro are currently reaching their end of support in October 2026. Pixel a-series phones are released on a different cadence, so support windows differ accordingly. The Pixel 7a will cease updates after May 2028, while the Pixel 6a will lose support after July 2027. 

The Pixel 8 and later are guaranteed to get seven years of support, meaning the Pixel 8 and 8 Pro will stop receiving updates after October 2030. It's thus still worth picking up a discounted Pixel 8 with the life it has in it. The Pixel 9 and 9 Pro (released in August-September 2024) will do the same after those months in 2031, the 2025 Pixel 10 and 10 Pro after August 2032, and the new Pixel 11 and 11 Pro after August 2033. 

The Pixel 8a, released in May 2024, will see support expire after May 2031. The Pixel 9a, which shipped in April 2025 after a March announcement, will receive no further updates after April 2032. Lastly, the Pixel 10a, which released slightly less than a year later, will receive a final update around March 2033.

...

If you want to keep your Pixel phone alive after Google kicks it off the update schedule, you have few options. Of course, you can keep using it with the last software update it receives, but this will expose your phone to security risks in the long run. Part of an Android phone's routine update schedule includes security patches, generally issued on a monthly cadence. Once those updates stop, new security issues that get discovered won't be fixed, leaving owners of older devices exposed. You should get a new phone if possible, or at least upgrade to one that still receives security updates.

title: These Google Pixel Phones No Longer Receive Software Support
text:
There are usually two major problems with old Google Pixel phones: degraded battery and discontinued software support. The battery issue can be resolved by getting a battery replacement for around $119 at a Google Store. But for the software support, phones are considered end-of-life once official updates stop. That's now the case for some Pixel phones. Every Google Pixel model from the Pixel 1 through the Pixel 5 series no longer gets official updates, meaning no more new features or security patches.

At this point, you have three options. You're free to still use the device as is, but without security updates, you'll soon find yourself in a vulnerable spot. Your device becomes more prone to malware, viruses, and hackers, and apps might stop working too. If you're comfortable tinkering with your phone's software, you can go with the custom OS route instead. This known loophole to unlock new updates for old Android phones essentially involves installing a completely new operating system on your device. It's a straightforward process, but can get quite technical. If you prefer to skip all that hassle, you can always upgrade to the newer Google Pixel phones that are still officially supported.

## Which Google Pixel phones still get updates?

In terms of software support, recently released Google Pixel phones can last seven years. So if you have a Pixel 8 and newer, you won't have to worry about missing out on any future Android updates. Google guarantees both OS and security updates for these devices for seven years from the date of their U.S. release. To be more specific, here's the end-of-life date for your Android phone, based on the model:

- Pixel 10a: March 2033
- Pixel 10 Pro Fold: October 2032
- Pixel 10, 10 Pro, and 10 Pro XL: August 2032
- Pixel 9a: April 2032
- Pixel 9 Pro and 9 Pro Fold: September 2031
- Pixel 9 and 9 Pro XL: August 2031
- Pixel 8a: May 2031
- Pixel 8 and Pixel 8 Pro: October 2030

Models newer than the Pixel 5 but older than the Pixel 8 still get updates today as well. But instead of seven years, they only receive five years of software support. Here's when these models will stop receiving updates:

- Pixel Fold: June 2028
- Pixel 7a: May 2028
- Pixel 7 and 7 Pro: October 2027
- Pixel 6a: July 2027
- Pixel 6 and 6 Pro: October 2026

That said, even though software support for these Google Pixel models is said to last five or seven years, don't expect to automatically get every single feature in the Pixel Drops. Some of them are hardware-specific and might not be compatible with every model.

In recent years, flagship Pixel phones have been released in October each year, followed by an additional mid-range variant known as the ‘A-series’ several months later. Since the introduction of Pixel 6 in 2021, Pixel phones have been supported with guaranteed Android version updates for three years and security updates for five years.

In October 2023, it was announced that Pixel 8 and Pixel 8 Pro will be guaranteed both Android version updates and security updates for seven years, offering full support until October 2030.

In December 2024, Google updated the information page for software updates to extend the support period for all Pixel 6 and Pixel 7 phones, as well as the Pixel Fold, to five years of both software and security updates.
